title: The Colony of Halcyon Drift
premise: Oscar Eriksen has spent a decade alone tending Earth's derelict seed vault, flying supply runs between colonies that severed contact after the Fracture War. When the name 'Vess Andrade' appears on the manifest of a ship that was destroyed years ago, Oscar discovers the two fleets' fragile truce rests on a forged manifest she is now legally bound to maintain — and Vess, alive and hiding aboard her own freighter, is the daughter of the admiral who started the war. As inspectors close in and both fleets mobilize on false intelligence, Oscar and Vess fall in love while keeping the lie alive; in the end, Oscar chooses to expose the truth at the Halcyon Drift summit, sacrificing her post and nearly her life, but forcing the fleets to negotiate peace with their real history instead of a comfortable fiction.
about_author: Noor Zhou is a former maritime logistics analyst who writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep vast systems running alone. She lives between ports and writes on trains, claiming the best sentences arrive at 40 knots.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes her solitary caretaking of the seed vault and her ritual supply run between silent colonies. The emotional beat is loneliness worn like routine — until she notices an impossible name, Vess Andrade, on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship lost six years ago.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghost
chapters.summary: Oscar investigates the anomaly, cross-checking archives that confirm the Meridian burned at Perseus Dock with all hands. The beat is creeping dread: someone is editing records, and only her terminal shows the original entry.

chapters.title: Stowaway at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She confronts the phantom ship and finds Vess Andrade alive, half-starved, hiding in the Meridian's restored hold. Vess begs for forty-eight hours before explaining. The beat is wary compassion overriding protocol.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Daughter
chapters.summary: Vess's POV flashback interwoven with present. She reveals she faked her death to escape being used as a war symbol by her father, Admiral Andrade, whose fleet still believes her martyrdom justifies the blockade. Beat: guilt and the weight of inherited power.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Oscar learns the truce holding the fleets apart depends on documents she certifies — including the Meridian's death record. If Vess is discovered alive, the ceasefire collapses. Beat: dawning responsibility; duty and mercy begin to pull apart.

chapters.title: Seed Vault Nights
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter. Vess helps Oscar tend the vault's germination bays while they wait out a solar storm. Found family begins here: two women building small rituals inside a machine built for extinction. Beat: tentative warmth.

chapters.title: Inspector Reyes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A fleet auditor arrives unannounced, sharp-eyed and courteous, asking about manifest discrepancies. Oscar lies for the first time in her career. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the lie becomes hers.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Exploring the vault's pre-war seed logs, she finds evidence her father falsified the incident that started the war. Beat: grief curdling into purpose — the truth could end the war, or ignite it worse.

chapters.title: Signal from Perseus
chapters.summary: A distress ping from the supposedly destroyed Perseus Dock reaches Oscar's array. Someone else survived, and they know Vess lives. Beat: the noose tightens; secrecy has a body count.

chapters.title: The Courier's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oscar meets the survivor, courier Ilsa Ren, who offers silence in exchange for passage off-world. Oscar must choose between buying safety with her savings or trusting a stranger. Beat: moral compromise; found family tested by necessity.

chapters.title: Inspection Day
chapters.summary: Reyes searches the Meridian while Vess hides in a cryo-bay. Oscar performs the performance of her life, nearly breaking when Reyes mentions the admiral by name. Beat: terror and its aftermath — Vess emerges, and something unspoken passes between them.

chapters.title: First Light in the Bays
chapters.summary: Slow-burn romance chapter. After the near-discovery, Oscar and Vess admit what the fear revealed. A kiss among sprouting seedlings. Beat: love against duty made literal — every hour together deepens the deception.

chapters.title: Orders from a Dead Ship
chapters.summary: Both fleets receive forged orders apparently originating from the Meridian, escalating toward confrontation at the Halcyon Drift neutral station. Someone is weaponizing Vess's ghost. Beat: realization they are pawns in a larger design.

chapters.title: Ilsa's True Cargo
chapters.summary: Oscar discovers Ilsa is an intelligence operative for the admiral, hunting his daughter. Confrontation in the vault corridors. Beat: betrayal, but also information — Ilsa confirms the summit will decide everything in nine days.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Planning chapter, dual POV. Oscar and Vess draft a dangerous plan: deliver the falsified war-origin evidence to both delegations simultaneously at Halcyon Drift. Beat: hope with teeth; love converted into strategy.

chapters.title: The Run to Halcyon
chapters.summary: Oscar flies the Meridian itself through the blockade, using its ghost-status as camouflage. Vess navigates. Near-misses with patrol ships. Beat: exhilaration and dread fused; the dead ship finally flies again.

chapters.title: Drift Station
chapters.summary: Arrival amid the summit's tense pageantry. They see the admirals face to face; Vess watches her father across a crowded concourse. Beat: dread of exposure, tenderness of a squeezed hand before separation.

chapters.title: The Evidence Burns
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Their data cache is seized in a sting — Ilsa's doing. With proof destroyed, Vess decides the only remaining evidence is herself. Beat: despair transmuting into courage.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Fracture
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Vess walks into the summit hall and reveals herself, testifying to her father's falsification while Oscar broadcasts the vault's raw seed logs as corroborating archive. Shots are fired; Oscar takes a wound shielding Vess. Beat: truth as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at Cost
chapters.summary: Falling action. The admiral's faction collapses; delegates sign an armistice grounded in verified records. Oscar recovers in the station infirmary, stripped of her caretaker certification. Beat: exhaustion, grief for the old life, relief.

chapters.title: Return to the Vault
chapters.summary: Oscar and Vess fly back to Earth not as fugitives but as witnesses, formally decommissioning the lie. Oscar plants the first open-registry seed row — grown for the future, not against it. Beat: mourning transformed into stewardship.

chapters.title: Halcyon, Growing
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. A year later: the vault is a shared trust tended by volunteers — a found family of gardeners, couriers, even a reformed Ilsa. Oscar and Vess take the long route together, by choice. Final beat: love and duty reconciled; the drift is home now.
